headline: Gold Slips Over 1% to $4,045 as Stronger US Dollar and Jobs Report Weaken Demand
summary: Spot gold dropped 1.02% to $4,045 per ounce on Friday as a robust US employment report boosted the dollar. Despite the daily pull-back, bullion tracked toward its strongest weekly performance since late August.
why: Gold is a benchmark global store of value that typically moves inversely to US dollar strength and Treasury yields.

impacts.name: Gold
impacts.why: A rising US dollar following upbeat labor market data reduced demand for non-yielding bullion.

why_moved: A strengthening US dollar following better-than-expected payroll data weighed on precious metals.
